newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AssiDoman says buys French Lecoursonnois.
newsitem.headline: AssiDoman says buys French Lecoursonnois.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Assidoman said on Wednesday it had bought French family-owned paper and corrugated board group Lecoursonnois, lifting its total annual corrugated packaging volume to 810,000 tonnes.
The acquisition also boosted the annual production of base paper for corrugated packaging to 1.18 million tonnes of liner and fluting, AssiDoman said in a statement.

"As a result of this strategically important acquisition of Lecoursonnois, we will have our own corrugated board capacity on the French market, which is the third largest in Europe," said chief executive Lennart Ahlgren.
"Together with our recent acquisition in Italy this strengthens our position considerably in the southern European region."
The French group consists of three wholly owned corrugated packaging plants, of which one is a sheet plant and one a wholly owned paper mill, AssiDoman said.
The total volume of corrugated board from the three plants amounts to 100 million square metres a year while the paper mill's capacity is 85,000 tonnes a year of waste-paper based liner and fluting.
The group has 450 employees and its 1997 sales from its units, all located in the Paris region, will total around 500 million crowns, AssiDoman said.

The acquisition also includes a 49.9 percent stake in Giepac Bourgogne, a 34 percent share in a sheet plant in Grenoble, Cartonnages du Dauphine, and a 20 percent stake in France-Flexo, a pre-print unit in the Paris area.
Giepac Bourgogne consists of five corrugated packaging plants and has an annual turnover of about 400 million crowns.
